rule: `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`. Generic/template type arguments are dropped from every ID (`HashSet#<init>`). Overloads share one ID. Companion-object members flatten onto the class. An ID is never invented: a medium or high callee that names a member of a scanned module or type (`mod.T#f`, `mod.f`) is defined there, or is inherited from a base outside the scan.
source: KNOWN_GAP: methods mixed into a companion from scanned traits stay medium
notes: The companion object Account flattens onto class Account and mixes in the scanned trait Logging. log is defined only on Logging, which is in the scan, so bare log(...) inside the object and Account.log(...) from Bank are app.Logging#log, high (self rule: 'defined only on a superclass that is in the scan'; C2: app.Account#log would be an invented ID, and medium is reserved for bases outside the scan). audit is defined in the object itself (implementing Audit's abstract member), so app.Account#audit. call_type convention used throughout: a call on a receiver (written, or the implicit this/object of a bare member call) is `method`; a call of a named nested function or an unresolved bare name is `direct`; `new`/super/this constructor calls are `constructor`; calls through function values are `callback`. SPEC lists the call_type values but does not define direct vs method beyond this.
